I am farming millet on this plot like I have done for many seasons. Here in the North West, the rains come once and we must plant when the ground is ready. I will buy a little fertilizer if the agro-dealer has it at a fair price, and I will spread the cattle manure I have collected over the dry season — that helps my soil more than chemicals alone. I keep my own seed from last year because the improved millet is hard to find here and costs too much. My sons help me with weeding and harvest, but I will hire a few hands for the heavy weeding when the rains are strong.
